messages:
alex: Quick q — we need to finalize the per-org rate policy knobs. My high-level: RPM + TPM + concurrency cap, plus a short grace/burst window that drains over a configurable window. Where should enforcement live (edge vs runtime) and what defaults make sense? :thinking:

maria: I like that. Proposed defaults (starter): RPM=1200, TPM=10_000, concurrency=20, burst_tokens=600, burst_window=120s. Soft limit first (429 + Retry-After), then hard drop if sustained. Example config snippet:

maria: ```
org_limits:
  default:
    rpm: 1200
    tpm: 10000
    concurrency: 20
    burst_tokens: 600
    burst_window_sec: 120
    enforcement: soft_then_hard
```

sam: Telemetry notes: we must emit per-org per-route counters + histogram of wait times and throttles. Need metrics for: soft_hits, hard_hits, avg_refill_rate, concurrency_peak. Also record events when soft->hard escalates for >1m.

june: Rollout plan idea: 48h dry-run (no 429s), surface affected orgs in Console with severity. Then enable soft-mode for 7d, then hard-mode. Legacy customers on old contracts get 30d migration. Also add per-org toggle in Console for temporary relief.

alex: Enforcement location: my vote = edge (api-gateway) for RPM/TPM to reject fast and save runtime cycles; runtime (inference proxy) for true per-model token accounting and concurrency caps. Edge can do token-bucket approximation for TPM. Agree?

maria: Yup. Edge token-bucket + header propagation (X-Org-Burst-Used, X-Org-Retry-After) so runtime can make final concurrency decisions. Edge returns early 429s for RPM/TMP.

sam: Small gotcha: token accounting needs to include streaming responses where tokens trickle out. Runtime should decrement concurrency only when connection fully closed or when final token count known. Otherwise we undercount.

june: UX: show "grace remaining" in Console and expose a short-lived token in header so clients can display to users. Also add an admin "grant burst" button for SEs.

alex: quota-bot, can you run the synthetic burst test we discussed and paste the numbers?

quota-bot: ran bulkload simulation against staging (org=acme-inc). config used: rpm=1200,tpm=10000,burst=600,window=120s. Results: avg_rpm=1_500, peak_rps=35, soft_limit_triggered=230s total, hard_limit_triggered=0s, max_concurrency=28. Observed client retry behavior increased p95 latency by ~180ms.

maria: That matches expectations — burst allowed short spikes but concurrency overshot. We should lower default concurrency to 16 or implement queue-with-timeout at runtime to keep pods safe.

sam: Also, add a costly-org flag for billing/alerts when soft hits > 5% of requests in a day. That helps ops contact customers before they hit hard limits.

june: For rollout: TODOs -> RFC doc with numbers, gateway PR for token-bucket edge impl, runtime change for streaming token accounting + concurrency queue, Console panel + per-org toggle, dry-run job, alert rules. I'll draft schedule.

alex: OK let's converge: change concurrency default to 16, keep burst_tokens=600 and burst_window=120s, keep TPM/RPM as proposed. I'll open the RFC and assign the TODOs. Thanks all :shipit:

maria: One more: add header X-RateLimit-Grace: <seconds_left> and X-RateLimit-Mode: soft|hard for easier client handling.

sam: And log an event when clients hit hard limit so CS can automate outreach.

june: I'll add rollout playbook for SEs (how to grant temporary relief, notify CS).

alex: Great. RFC link incoming from me in ~1h.
